title: Bodh Gaya and the Mahabodhi Temple Complex
summary: Site in Bihar where, by Buddhist tradition, Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under a bodhi tree. Tradition credits Ashoka with a first temple in the 3rd century BCE; the present brick Mahabodhi Temple dates to about the 5th to 6th century CE and was heavily restored in the 19th century.

uncertainty.note: Start is Ashoka's reported first temple (ASI: around 260 B.C.; UNESCO: 3rd century B.C.). The present temple is later (5th-6th century CE). End is the present.

as_recorded.value: Emperor Asoka visited Bodh Gaya around 260 B.C. and constructed a small temple; present temple may be datable to the 6th century A.D.
first temple built by Emperor Asoka in the 3rd century B.C.; present temple dates from the 5th-6th centuries

when.display: Ashokan temple from c. 260 BCE (tradition); present temple c. 5th-6th century CE

where.modern_name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya, Gaya district, Bihar, India
where.historical_name: Uruvela, in the Magadha region (traditional); site of Ashoka's Mauryan temple in the 3rd century BCE

importance.justification: One of the four holy sites of the Buddha's life and among the oldest standing brick temples in India.

sources.title: Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya (World Heritage List no. 1056)
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: No 3D model written: UNESCO gives the temple as 50 m high and the ASI says 55 m, and no opened page gives a plan dimension.
